question.title: Tell me about a time you improved system reliability.
question.description: Behavioral question probing ownership and measurable impact.

cases.answer: Last year our checkout service had 14 Sev-2 incidents in one quarter. I owned the reliability workstream: I added distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry, set SLOs at 99.9% availability, and built a runbook for the top 5 failure modes. We cut incidents from 14 per quarter to 2, and p99 latency dropped from 900ms to 320ms. I learned that writing the postmortem template first made every review faster.

question.title: Explain caching trade-offs for a read-heavy API.
question.description: Technical question probing depth and trade-off reasoning.

cases.answer: For read-heavy workloads I would start with cache-aside using Redis: reads hit the cache first and fall through to the database on a miss. The trade-off is stale reads during the TTL window, so for inventory counts I would use write-through instead. I would add a short TTL of 60 seconds for product listings and monitor the hit ratio; below 80% I would revisit key granularity before adding more memory.

mustQuote: stale reads during the TTL window

cases.answer: I would use a token bucket per API key in Redis. That handles bursts well.
